questions.question: Which action best improves the reliability of online information?
choices: Rely on the first search result
Check author/date and cross-reference multiple sources
Share it to see if others agree
Use only social media posts
questions.explanation: Reliability increases with provenance checks and triangulation across independent sources.

questions.question: In a spreadsheet, what is the safest first step before cleaning a large dataset?
choices: Delete duplicates immediately
Sort the data to see patterns
Make a copy (backup) of the original data
Change number formats across all columns
questions.explanation: Always preserve the original dataset before applying irreversible operations.

questions.question: You need to co-edit a document with comments and version history. What is the best approach?
choices: Send updated attachments by email after every change
Use a shared cloud document with permissions, comments, and version history
Ask one person to edit while others wait
Copy/paste edits into a chat thread
questions.explanation: Shared documents support concurrent editing, permissions, traceability, and recovery.

questions.question: A colleague shares a file link. What is a good practice before forwarding it externally?
choices: Forward it immediately if it works
Check the sharing permissions and whether the link exposes sensitive content
Download it and re-upload it publicly
Convert it to an image and send it
questions.explanation: Verify access controls and content sensitivity to prevent unintended disclosure.

questions.question: What is the best way to ensure a presentation remains readable on a projector?
choices: Use small text to fit more content
Use high contrast and limit text per slide
Use many animations to keep attention
Use low-contrast colors to look modern
questions.explanation: Projectors and room lighting reduce legibility; contrast and simplicity improve readability.

questions.question: When creating a document to be reused by others, what is the most effective step?
choices: Use random formatting so it stands out
Define styles (headings, body text) to ensure consistency
Disable spellcheck
Avoid templates and reuse
questions.explanation: Styles and templates enforce consistency and make updates scalable.

questions.question: A colleague asks you to share a file containing personal data via a public link. What is the safest default?
choices: Share the public link immediately
Encrypt the file but keep the link public
Use restricted access (named users) and least-privilege permissions
Upload it to a forum with a password
questions.explanation: Least privilege + restricted access reduces leakage risk and improves accountability.

questions.question: Which password practice is generally the strongest?
choices: Reuse a complex password everywhere
Use a long unique passphrase and a password manager
Change passwords daily
Use your name plus a number
questions.explanation: Unique long passphrases plus a manager reduce reuse risk and are easier to maintain.

questions.question: A spreadsheet formula returns an error after you copy it down. What is the most likely fix?
choices: Convert the sheet to PDF
Use absolute/relative references appropriately (e.g., $A$1 vs A1)
Increase the font size
Disable automatic calculation
questions.explanation: Copying formulas often requires adjusting cell references to preserve intended references.

questions.question: A video meeting has echo and feedback. What is a good first troubleshooting step?
choices: Increase speaker volume to overpower the echo
Ask everyone to unmute
Identify a participant using speakers and switch them to headphones or mute their speakers
Turn off the camera
questions.explanation: Echo is commonly caused by a mic picking up the speaker output; headphones/muting fixes it.
